originalText: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन | मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ||
translation: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself to be the cause of the results of your activities, and never be attached to not doing your duty.
context: On decision paralyses, anxiety about outcomes, and working with dedication without being obsessed with the results.

originalText: क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोह: सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रम: | स्मृतिभ्रंशाद्बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ||
translation: From anger arises complete delusion, and from delusion bewilderment of memory. When memory is bewildered, intellect is lost, and when intellect is lost, one is ruined.
context: On control of anger, emotional reactivity, and preserving rational intelligence during crisis.

originalText: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुण: परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् | स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेय: परधर्मो भयावह: ||
translation: It is far better to perform one's own naturally prescribed duty, even though imperfectly, than another's duty perfectly. Destruction in the course of performing one's own duty is better than engaging in another's, for following another's path is dangerous.
context: On authenticity, finding one's unique vocation, identity crises, and resisting societal peer pressure.

originalText: ईशा वास्यमिदं सर्वं यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत् | तेन त्यक्तेन भुञ्जीथा मा गृधः कस्यस्विद्धनम् ||
translation: All this—whatever moves in this moving world—is enveloped by the Divine. Therefore, find your enjoyment in renunciation; do not covet what belongs to others.
context: On greed, sustainable living, contentment, sharing wealth, and ethical wealth acquisition.

originalText: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् | आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मन: ||
translation: One must elevate oneself by one's own mind, and not degrade oneself. For the mind is the friend of the self, and the mind is the enemy of the self as well.
context: On self-reliance, mental health, depression, personal accountability, and conquering self-doubt.

originalText: Μὴ οὖν μεριμνήσητε εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἡ γὰρ αὔριον μεριμνήσει ἑαυτῆς· ἀρκετὸν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἡ κακία αὐτῆς.
translation: Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
context: On relieving chronic anxiety, future insecurity, and focusing energy on immediate moral actions.

originalText: καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως.
translation: Do to others as you would have them do to you.
context: The Golden Rule of reciprocal ethics, empathy, fairness in business, and resolving interpersonal conflicts.

originalText: μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ, ἀλλὰ νίκα ἐν τῷ ἀγαθῷ τὸ κακόν.
translation: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
context: On dealing with enemies, betrayal, reactive vengeance, and selecting a constructive retaliatory response.

originalText: τί γὰρ ὠφεληθήσεται ἄνθρωπος ἐὰν τὸν κόσμον ὅλον κερδήσῃ τὴν δὲ ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ζημιωθῇ;
translation: What good will it be for someone to gain the whole world, yet forfeit their soul? Or what can anyone give in exchange for their soul?
context: On priority of moral value over material gain, maintaining integrity in corporate greed.

originalText: τὸ δὲ καλὸν ποιοῦντες μὴ ἐγκακῶμεν, καιρῷ γὰρ ἰδίῳ θερίσομεν μὴ ἐκλυόμενοι.
translation: Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.
context: On persistent social action, overcoming discouragement, burn-out in philanthropy, and resilience.

originalText: मनोपुब्बङ्गमा धम्मा मनोसेट्ठा मनोमया। मनसा चे पदुट्ठेन भासति वा करोति वा। ततो नं दुक्खमन्वेति चक्कंव वहतो पदं।।
translation: Mind precedes all mental states. Mind is their chief; they are mind-made. If one speaks or acts with an impure mind, suffering follows him close behind, like the wheel follows the hoof of the ox.
context: On the ultimate gravity of intent, mindfulness before speaking, and personal karma.

originalText: न हि वेरेन वेरानि सम्मन्तीध कुदाचनं। अवेरेन च सम्मन्ति एस धम्मो सनन्तनो।।
translation: Hatred is never appeased by hatred in this world. By non-hatred alone is hatred appeased. This is a law eternal.
context: On resolving feuds, hatred, political divisions, disputes, and radiating unconditional compassion.

originalText: आरोग्यपरमा लाभा सन्तुट्ठीपरमं धनं। विस्सासपरमा ञाती निब्बानं परमं सुखं।।
translation: Health is the greatest of gifts, contentment the greatest wealth; trust is the best of relationships, Nirvana the highest happiness.
context: On minimal living, avoiding excessive consumerism, building relational trust, and mental health.

originalText: माता यथा नियं पुत्तं आयुसा एकपुत्तमनुरक्खे। एवम्पि सब्बभूतेसु मानसं भावये अपरिमाणं।।
translation: Even as a mother would protect her only child with her life, so too let one cultivate a limitless heart of goodwill towards all beings.
context: On empathy, expanding care beyond family to colleagues and global beings, selfless protection.

originalText: तुम्हेहि किच्चं आतप्पं अक्खातारो तथागता। पटिपन्ना पमोक्खन्ति झायिनो मारबन्धना।।
translation: You yourselves must strive; the Buddhas only point the way. Those who meditate and enter the path are freed from the bonds of death.
context: On taking active responsibility instead of expecting external miracle rescues in moral crises.

originalText: لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ
translation: Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned.
context: On dealing with overwhelming stress, heavy responsibilities, severe life trials, and ethical limits.

originalText: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَاءَ بِالْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا ۚ اعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ
translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness.
context: On systemic justice, refusing subjective favoritism, holding truth even against personal interests or enemies.

originalText: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا • إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
translation: For indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease.
context: On comforting those going through business failures, sorrow, bereavement, or difficult transitions.

originalText: وَلَا تَسْتَوِي الْحَسَنَةُ وَلَا السَّيِّئَةُ ۚ ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ فَإِذَا الَّذِي بَيْنَكَ وَبَيْنَهُ عَدَاوَةٌ كَأَنَّهُ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ
translation: And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel [evil] by that which is better; and thereupon, the one whom between you and him is enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend.
context: On conflict de-escalation, turning rivals into friends, active kindness, and professional diplomacy under pressure.

originalText: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِّنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ ۖ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلَا يَغْتَب بَّعْضُكُم بَّعْضًا
translation: O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Indeed, some assumption is sin. And do not spy or backbite each other.
context: On trust, workplace toxic gossip, respect for privacy, and emotional boundaries.
